Latitude-width experiments must be interpreted separately from cell-resolution experiments. The early coarse ±30°/±60° comparison changes flux by approximately 14%; that is measured sensitivity, not a validated ±14% uncertainty bound. Comparisons of different numerical fluxes also need to remain separate from domain comparisons. Exact-GLM preprocessing with the original dissipation changes the coarse PN flux by less than 1%, whereas a split GLM treatment with lower transverse dissipation can change it much more. This numerical-method dependence must not be hidden behind a single successful refinement test. Full divergence and scheme diagnostics; independent domain assessment.

GLM cleaning leaves nonzero magnetic divergence. The medium comet-neighborhood h|div B|/|B| decreases from about 0.018 to 0.006, and its nearest-cell value is about 0.003. A monopole-force scale is small relative to bulk inertia, but that ratio is not a rigorous accumulated-flux error bound. These calculations do not establish a converged magnetic topology. Coarse controls below quantify changing B, temperature, speed, density and γ; they are sensitivity experiments with the same coarse grid, not uncertainty percentiles.
